## concept

### A Non-Zero Chance Beats Zero
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

The arithmetic that keeps the pattern running. A house with heating ten per cent of the time still beats an outdoors with none, so it is rational to stay inside and work on the boiler. Priebe's point is that the fixation on getting a dysregulated partner regulated again is not irrational attachment — it is the only option with a probability above zero, and the unconscious has done the maths.

  - part_of → The Intimacy Desert (https://youtu.be/TLiZDks_vlU?t=450)
  - mirrors → Monitoring The Bond (https://youtu.be/TLiZDks_vlU?t=500)
  - source: Fearful-Avoidant: How Intimacy Scarcity Keeps You Codependent (And How To Change It) @450s — https://youtu.be/TLiZDks_vlU?t=450

### A Pervasive Sense Of Self
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form*

Holding an account of who you are that does not require confirmation from the conversation you are currently in. With it, being misunderstood is temporary and survivable; without it, disagreement lands as an identity threat, and what someone else believes about you becomes something you have to win.

  - part_of → Realistic Cause And Effect (https://youtu.be/Us1a6N7jNg0?t=226)
  - contrasts_with → I Am Not Okay And Neither Are You (https://youtu.be/Us1a6N7jNg0?t=226)
  - source: Cultivating The Ability To Tolerate Emotional Discomfort @226s — https://youtu.be/Us1a6N7jNg0?t=226
  - characterizes → Secure (https://youtu.be/Us1a6N7jNg0?t=226)

### A Reasonable Need Is Not An Obligation
*concept · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The anxious version of fairness runs: if what I want is reasonable, they ought to provide it. Priebe declines the inference. Your need can be entirely reasonable and this person can still be unwilling — and what you hold is not a claim on them but the choice of who you are with. If the pattern repeats across partners, the question moves to how much you are routing through one relationship.

  - part_of → Nobody Is Required To Give You Their Attention (https://youtu.be/0GeM7bT_nyY?t=760)
  - mirrors → Setting A Boundary You Control (https://youtu.be/0GeM7bT_nyY?t=790)
  - contrasts_with → I Cannot Be Okay Until They Change (https://youtu.be/0GeM7bT_nyY?t=800)
  - source: Anxious Attachment: 5 Questions To Ask Yourself Before Getting Back Together With An Ex @760s — https://youtu.be/0GeM7bT_nyY?t=760

### Accidental Bad Faith
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Her central coinage here. In law or debate, arguing in bad faith means knowingly pushing an agenda other than the stated one. In an insecure dynamic the same structure appears without the knowing: the real want is hidden from the person holding it. Functionally it behaves identically — the stated issue never resolves, because neither party is actually arguing about it.

  - source: The Real Reason Why Most Anxious-Avoidant Relationships Fail (And How To Combat It) @393s — https://youtu.be/P8D5y4nrVRw?t=393
  - part_of → Unconscious Relationship Premise (https://youtu.be/P8D5y4nrVRw?t=513)

### Accidental Intimacy
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

The fearful-avoidant keeps the shame-bound material — which is to say, ordinary human emotion — out of every social and professional setting, and it surfaces only where self-control fails: inside a close relationship, under trigger. So the one experience of being fully known arrives as a by-product of the worst moments, and belongs exclusively to the relationship that produced them.

  - part_of → The Intimacy Desert (https://youtu.be/TLiZDks_vlU?t=200)
  - contrasts_with → Sensitizing, Then Sharing (https://youtu.be/TLiZDks_vlU?t=1000)
  - source: Fearful-Avoidant: How Intimacy Scarcity Keeps You Codependent (And How To Change It) @140s — https://youtu.be/TLiZDks_vlU?t=140

### Adaptive Versus Healthy
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Something can be exactly right for the situation that produced it and ruinous over a lifetime. Priebe insists the insecure strategy was the correct answer to the home it was formed in — not a defect, not stupidity — and that the only route to a healthier response runs through understanding what environment you were solving for.

### All My Exes Were Narcissists
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Priebe refuses this as an answer to what has gone wrong before — not because it is never true of any individual, but because as an account of a pattern it names the obstacle and then declines to work on it. If the partners keep turning out that way, the thing in the way is what you are drawn to, and that is the item on the list before the next relationship.

### Allergic To The Medicine
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The avoidant needs love as much as anyone and reacts badly to it in quantity, so it has to be taken in small amounts and spaced out. That is the shape of the slow approach — a little closeness, then distance to manage the reaction, then a little more — repeated for years. Intimacy is the trigger because intimacy once meant your boundaries were about to go.

  - part_of → The Emotional Immune System (https://youtu.be/ZZOVY0HTpxU?t=1100)
  - characterizes → Dismissive-Avoidant (https://youtu.be/ZZOVY0HTpxU?t=1240)

  - source: The 4 Attachment Styles In Relationships @1100s — https://youtu.be/ZZOVY0HTpxU?t=1100

### An Unspoken Boundary Guarantees A Repeat
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Slipping away, going quiet and hoping the other person works it out leaves them with no information, so the next attempt comes with more force — and the situation recurs at higher intensity. Priebe's structure for the avoidant is that the end of the sequence is right (go and regulate alone) and the middle is missing: say what is wrong, what is unacceptable, and what would need to change.

  - characterizes → Dismissive-Avoidant (https://youtu.be/yPDW4GTl2C0?t=740)
  - mirrors → Detaching Is Not A Boundary (https://youtu.be/yPDW4GTl2C0?t=700)
  - contrasts_with → Naming The Conflict And Your Intent (https://youtu.be/yPDW4GTl2C0?t=780)
  - source: The 4 Attachment Styles Setting Boundaries @740s — https://youtu.be/yPDW4GTl2C0?t=740

### Anger Is Self-Correcting
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Stated the first time a line is crossed, anger usually stops the crossing. Stated the tenth time, it arrives alongside nine occasions on which you said nothing — which weakens your own footing, because you were the one who let it stand. The function of anger is corrective, and it only performs that function on time.

  - part_of → The Anger Scale (https://youtu.be/QFrkbdUIYFM?t=480)
  - contrasts_with → Introducing Old Grievances (https://youtu.be/QFrkbdUIYFM?t=520)

### Asking For Help Feels Natural
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form · sign of change*

Needs were met early without having to be exaggerated or fought for, so the adult expects the same ordinary reciprocation: I say what I need, you supply it if you can, and if you cannot you say so. The insecure styles find asking hard and receiving harder. Priebe notes the secure person also gives help readily, which is part of why asking feels unremarkable.

### Attunement
*concept · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Reading another person's state, letting your own respond to it, and reflecting it back accurately before helping settle it. Her image is a caregiver meeting a crying infant with a face that matches the distress rather than contradicts it — the child sees its inner state confirmed, and only then soothed.

  - contrasts_with → Misattuned Mirroring (https://youtu.be/TplLHhDRqAQ?t=200)
  - source: Learning Self-Regulation Through Self-Attunement @200s — https://youtu.be/TplLHhDRqAQ?t=200
  - source: Attunement: How Securely Attached People Develop Intimacy @60s — https://youtu.be/fBiSDVPF0dg?t=60

### Attunement Is Not Only The Loud Signal
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Priebe's answer to the standard objection — that attending to your feelings would make you irrational and idle. She borrows the intuitive-eating case: the fear is that you would live on pizza, but genuine attunement includes noticing which foods leave you flat and which are easy on you. Emotionally the same holds. The system that says stay in bed is also the system that wants to feel proud of itself and will supply the discipline.

  - mirrors → Treating Emotion As Data (https://youtu.be/lsBPvgnCJsQ?t=500)
  - contrasts_with → Anything That Feels Bad Is Bad (https://youtu.be/lsBPvgnCJsQ?t=560)
  - part_of → Feelings Are Data, Not Noise (https://youtu.be/lsBPvgnCJsQ?t=600)
  - source: Emotional Neglect: Healing From The Hidden Trauma Of What Didn't Happen @500s — https://youtu.be/lsBPvgnCJsQ?t=500

### Avoidance Is A Misnomer
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

To avoid a thing you have to know it is there. Priebe's objection to the label is that the dismissive type is mostly not declining to look — the painful thought does not reach awareness at all. Conscious avoidance of distressing thoughts is more characteristic of the anxious and fearful-avoidant types. Her own names would be closer to oblivious and obsessive, which she concedes would not catch on.

  - part_of → Not A Personality Type (https://youtu.be/4avJofwpVNw?t=250)
  - contrasts_with → Deactivating Strategies (https://youtu.be/4avJofwpVNw?t=260)
  - source: Anxious vs Avoidant Attachment Styles & Emotional Pain @250s — https://youtu.be/4avJofwpVNw?t=250

### Avoidants Are Not Villains
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Popular attachment writing tends to sympathise with the anxious style and warn people away from the avoidant one. Priebe rejects that split: the avoidant adaptation is as involuntary and as early as the anxious one, and describing it as a character flaw makes it harder for avoidant people to recognise themselves in the material at all.

  - derived_from → Thais Gibson (https://youtu.be/AMUN9M9H3U4?t=1660)

  - source: What Are The 4 Attachment Styles? @1660s — https://youtu.be/AMUN9M9H3U4?t=1660

### Awareness Is Not The Solution
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

A correction Priebe returns to across her work and states plainly here: people reaching stage two assume that because they can see the problem they should be able to solve it, and conclude something is wrong with them when they cannot. Seeing it and being able to do otherwise are separate acquisitions, and the gap between them is the healing process rather than a failure inside it.

  - part_of → Knowing The Mechanism (https://youtu.be/GbWAlMQkWzo?t=300)
  - contrasts_with → Conscious Competence (https://youtu.be/GbWAlMQkWzo?t=480)
  - source: The 4 Stages Of Attachment Healing (Conscious Competency Model) @300s — https://youtu.be/GbWAlMQkWzo?t=300

### Babies Cannot Be Manipulative
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Priebe stops to rule this out explicitly. An infant lacks the equipment for manipulation; it is running trial and error and keeping whatever works. If expressing the real feeling was punished and expressing a different one was rewarded, the child learns the substitution without ever forming the intention. The same behaviour in an adult, with adult capacities, is another matter.

  - part_of → Adaptive Versus Healthy (https://youtu.be/sUgQ_E24ma0?t=140)
  - contrasts_with → Using The Framework To Manipulate (https://youtu.be/sUgQ_E24ma0?t=175)
  - source: Are Fearful-Avoidants Doomed To Have Dysfunctional Relationships? @140s — https://youtu.be/sUgQ_E24ma0?t=140

### Balancing Pain With An Extreme High
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

The fearful-avoidant feels pain at anxious volume and co-regulates like an avoidant — which is to say, barely. Unable to sit with it and unwilling to be vulnerable about it, they offset it with something large: the sudden travel, the enormous ambition, the extravagant redirection. Priebe notes all insecure styles cope badly at times; what is specific here is having the anxious level of pain with the avoidant level of support.

  - derived_from → Scattered Minds (https://youtu.be/5jk7PAa8D1o?t=3180)
  - contrasts_with → Tolerating Emotional Discomfort (https://youtu.be/5jk7PAa8D1o?t=3240)
  - source: 10 Signs You May Have A Fearful-Avoidant Attachment Style @3130s — https://youtu.be/5jk7PAa8D1o?t=3130

### Base Strategy With Trauma Intrusions
*concept · literature · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

One account of fearful-avoidant development that Priebe finds useful: a single base strategy — say, avoidant — with trauma triggers that periodically flip the system into its opposite. Downplay everything most of the time; then a flashback arrives and the response overshoots into amplification or aggression. Run often enough, it stops looking like intrusions and starts looking like a style.

  - part_of → Disorganized Attachment (https://youtu.be/sUgQ_E24ma0?t=380)
  - characterizes → Fearful-Avoidant (https://youtu.be/sUgQ_E24ma0?t=400)
  - contrasts_with → Holding Both Programs (https://youtu.be/sUgQ_E24ma0?t=420)
  - source: Are Fearful-Avoidants Doomed To Have Dysfunctional Relationships? @380s — https://youtu.be/sUgQ_E24ma0?t=380

### Becoming Worthy Of Someone Self-Sufficient
*concept · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The anxious appraisal of a new person is an audit of what they have that you lack — charm, confidence, ease — and a private conclusion that you will never have it, but could acquire it by being loved by someone who does. Hence the paradox: real investment in self-improvement, aimed not at becoming self-sufficient but at becoming the sort of person a self-sufficient person would choose.

### Being Accurately Decoded
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Her metaphor for what an infant is actually up against: waking on an unfamiliar planet with a single guide who controls everything you need, and only emotion to communicate with. A guide fluent in your language is a relief; one who catches a tenth of it is frightening. The two insecure strategies are the two available responses to being misread — send the signal harder, or stop sending and go looking alone.

  - part_of → Attunement (https://youtu.be/9mOGpwcAfKk?t=482)
  - mirrors → Emotions As Currency (https://youtu.be/9mOGpwcAfKk?t=602)
  - source: Early Experiences Of The Secure Attachment Style @602s — https://youtu.be/9mOGpwcAfKk?t=602

### Being Idealised Is Comfortable And Costly
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

A partner who finds you flawless confirms the I-am-okay-you-are-not model, and is therefore easy to be around — and cannot tolerate it when you eventually bring something real. Meanwhile a secure partner noticing where you are struggling registers as criticism, or as being found insufficient, when it is usually just attention. Priebe's ask is to get comfortable being seen whole, unfinished parts included.

### Being The Same Person Everywhere
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form*

Her stated end point for fearful-avoidant healing. The test she offers is concrete: how a partner would describe you should broadly match how friends, family and colleagues would. Her image for the mechanism is oxygen — parts of us kept shut away go strange in the dark and emerge strangely; exposed a little at a time to people who can be trusted with them, they grow into something ordinary.

  - characterizes → Secure (https://youtu.be/gqPnXU_JKOk?t=1332)
  - contrasts_with → The Social Mask (https://youtu.be/gqPnXU_JKOk?t=1574)

  - source: Fearful-Avoidant: The Blindspot That Keeps You Repeating The Same Relationship Mistakes @1332s — https://youtu.be/gqPnXU_JKOk?t=1332

### Better Is A Relational Skill
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Insecure attachment tends to read self-improvement as raising your score on visible variables — fitness, money, being interesting. Priebe's claim is that those recruit people who also rank on those variables and do not know how to connect. What actually makes healthy love available is the capacity to stay regulated while holding someone else's complexity, including the parts of it that threaten you.

### Blaming The Relationship For What You Stopped Doing
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Priebe's own repeated pattern: disciplined about health and work when single, and then, on entering any relationship, unconsciously avoiding all conflict and putting her own needs behind her partner's — until one day she looked across and concluded he was why her career had stalled. The partner had not asked for any of it. The abandonment was hers, and it made the fantasy of leaving look correct.

  - part_of → The Exit Fantasy (https://youtu.be/yPDW4GTl2C0?t=1340)
  - mirrors → Deactivation As A Response To Your Own Rules (https://youtu.be/yPDW4GTl2C0?t=1300)
  - contrasts_with → Keeping Your Life Outside The Relationship (https://youtu.be/yPDW4GTl2C0?t=1400)
  - source: The 4 Attachment Styles Setting Boundaries @1340s — https://youtu.be/yPDW4GTl2C0?t=1340

### Both Feel They Give More
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The anxious partner gives constantly and feels unvalued, because what is given is the thing the other is allergic to. The avoidant partner keeps themselves level through everything life throws and feels unvalued too, because they are also expected to absorb someone else's crises. Priebe's observation is that in these pairings both people believe, accurately from where they stand, that they are carrying it.

  - mirrors → Projecting Your Own Remedy (https://youtu.be/ZZOVY0HTpxU?t=1500)
  - part_of → How Is This Adaptive In Our Dynamic (https://youtu.be/ZZOVY0HTpxU?t=1520)

  - source: The 4 Attachment Styles In Relationships @1500s — https://youtu.be/ZZOVY0HTpxU?t=1500

### Boundary
*concept · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

A decision about what you will do, enforceable no matter what anyone else chooses. Her test is ownership: a boundary is a fence built on your own side of the property line, so nobody else can take it down. If keeping it requires someone else to behave a particular way, it is not one.

  - contrasts_with → Expectation (https://youtu.be/9WzGv5SNgBQ?t=90)
  - source: Attachment Vocabulary: Boundaries vs Expectations @2s — https://youtu.be/9WzGv5SNgBQ?t=2

### Changing The Environment, Not Just The Response
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Half of the work is behaving securely in the situations you are already in. The other half is noticing which situations you selected because the old strategy handles them, and moving. Priebe's line is that you cannot get healthy while unprotected in a sick environment — trying to be secure where insecure responses are genuinely the most adaptive is not a fair test of anything.

  - part_of → Where The Strategy Still Works (https://youtu.be/sUgQ_E24ma0?t=700)

  - source: Are Fearful-Avoidants Doomed To Have Dysfunctional Relationships? @700s — https://youtu.be/sUgQ_E24ma0?t=700

### Chosen Excitement
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form*

Her answer to the worry that security is flat. The intensity of insecure attachment is largely reactive — you are responding to whatever temporarily makes you feel alright. With a stable baseline, the adventure is selected rather than arriving at you, and she rates the two as not really comparable.

  - characterizes → Secure (https://youtu.be/HHJ1dKAL18Y?t=485)
  - contrasts_with → Security Will Be Boring (https://youtu.be/HHJ1dKAL18Y?t=485)

### Closeness Is Not Sameness
*concept · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Priebe's improv story makes the point better than the theory does. A friendship had gone flat while she deferred to what the other person wanted; in a class exercise where each character held a private objective, the interplay came straight back. Wanting something that had nothing to do with his approval was what put energy between them. Intimacy needs edges — otherwise nobody can tell where one of you stops.

### Co-Regulation
*concept · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Two nervous systems settling each other. Mostly mundane — getting used to someone replying, to their presence in a week — rather than the dramatic comforting the word suggests, which is why becoming dependent on it goes unnoticed.

### Co-Regulation Toward Independence
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form*

Her sharpest distinction in this video: much of what passes for co-regulation in insecure relationships is the drama triangle with one partner rescuing. The secure version leaves both people more able to manage, not less — closeness offered as a reminder of what you can do, rather than as the thing standing in for it.

  - characterizes → Secure (https://youtu.be/WKof0naxYLM?t=204)
  - contrasts_with → Saviour Position (https://youtu.be/WKof0naxYLM?t=204)
  - source: 6 Qualities Of A Securely Attached Relationship @204s — https://youtu.be/WKof0naxYLM?t=204

### Comfort From Someone Other Than The One Who Hurt You
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

The wound underneath fearful-avoidance is having needed comfort from the person causing the distress, with no alternative available. The belief that follows is that only the source of the pain can relieve it. Priebe treats breaking that specific link — learning to seek real support outside the relationship the trouble is in — as the single highest-leverage move available to the style.

### Commitment As A Life Sentence Of Self-Erasure
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Priebe's reframe of avoidant commitment fear. If being in a relationship means obeying the rulebook, then committing means obeying it for life — and the resistance is accurate. Secure people commit easily not because they are braver but because they are not betraying themselves: when an arrangement stops working they renegotiate it. The fear is of the terms, not of the person.

### Compartmentalising Yourself To Stay
*concept · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Entering a relationship having decided in advance which parts of you will not appear, on the grounds that the whole version would not be accepted. Priebe puts it in the harshest terms she uses anywhere: it tells the most vulnerable part of you that it can be traded for someone else's approval, and it works on self-esteem over years the way you would expect.

  - mirrors → Becoming What They Want (https://youtu.be/0GeM7bT_nyY?t=540)

### Complex Causality
*concept · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The security position, and the exit from the blame see-saw: most conflicts are produced by two people acting in good faith whose triggers and unexamined programmes collide. Not because either is malicious, but because communicating across two histories is difficult and needs continuous renegotiation. Priebe calls the alternative — one of you is doing it all wrong — a false dichotomy in both directions.

### Compliance Without Agreement
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

A relationship where the instructions get carried out and the resentment quietly builds. She names it as the failure mode of solving a conflict on one person's terms: agreement reached by collaboration is the only kind either party actually wants to keep.

### Conflict Is Uncomfortable, Not Catastrophic
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form · sign of change*

Secure people generally do not enjoy conflict and are willing to have it, because they either saw it resolved peacefully or learned later that it can be. Priebe's sharpest observation is about what the insecure styles are missing: not the courage but the knowledge — at a gut level they do not know that a direct conversation which simply settles something is an available outcome.

### Conscious Competence
*concept · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Being able to notice the trigger and do something other than the old thing — with full effort, every time, against what feels like your own grain. Priebe says this stage often takes years and is the one people quit in, and that the feedback loop back into stage two is normal rather than a relapse.

### Conscious Incompetence
*concept · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Seeing the problem clearly and having none of the equipment to solve it — which Priebe rates the most frustrating stage of the four, because the awareness arrives long before the capacity does. Its actual job is observation: when the triggering happens, what precedes it, which parts of life it reaches. People want to skip it and cannot.

### Consciously Adapting To Each Relationship
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form · sign of change*

Feeling avoidant around some people and anxious around others is not evidence of fearful-avoidance — most people pull back a little from a surplus of anxious energy and lean in a little toward someone who gives them nothing to read. Secure people do the same thing deliberately: take a little space here, try a bit harder there, without an outer critic and without insult when a text goes unanswered.

### Containment
*concept · literature · secure=secure-form*

Holding another person's experience in your own mind in a way they cannot yet, running it through an adult's processing, and handing back something they can use. Absorb, mirror accurately, then help them find a response. A child arrives with no template for anger or sadness and learns what to do with it from what comes back.

### Controlling How Your Partner Feels About You
*concept · literature · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Priebe notes the gap between the popular picture of anxious attachment — sympathetic, deprived of love — and what the literature actually describes, which is controlling. Not usually overt: the control is over how the partner feels, so that they stay aligned and connected and the co-regulation stays available. She adds that you would be hard pressed to find an anxious person who recognises it, because it runs below the level of choice.

### Deactivation As A Response To Your Own Rules
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Priebe's worked example. A long-distance partner was going to visit; within days she was cataloguing everything wrong with them and losing attraction. What had actually happened was a rule switching on — while they are in my space I may not ask for time alone, refuse closeness, or have needs of my own — and the disgust was a response to that sentence, which her partner had never uttered. The rules were hers, and she had assigned them to him.

### Decision Paralysis And The Empty Milestone
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Emotions are what tell you what matters, so losing access to them breaks decision-making at both scales. At the large scale you follow other people's formula for a good life, hit the milestones, and cannot work out why arriving feels like nothing. At the small scale you can spend an hour on dinner or a shirt, because with no guiding principles the only available signal is the next small hit.

### Detaching Is Not A Boundary
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Avoidant people often believe their boundaries are excellent because they are very good at detaching. Priebe separates the two: detaching is a trauma response, and a boundary is being clear about a need, saying what the limit is and why, and then living inside it. Boundaries make interdependence possible; detachment produces counter-dependence, which is a different thing wearing the same word.

### Differentiation
*concept · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Knowing where you end and another person begins — which feeling in the room is yours. An infant cannot yet tell itself apart from its caregiver, and where that separation is never properly completed, the adult keeps mistaking their own state for someone else's.

  - source: How Does An Anxious Attachment Style Develop? @966s — https://youtu.be/EdpaCMW1PHw?t=966

### Direction Of Travel
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Each insecure style is moving toward something it never arrives at. The anxious person is going for relationship security and keeps finding another floor below the one they reached. The avoidant person is going for complete self-sufficiency. The fearful-avoidant has no settled direction at all — approach and exit alternate — which is why the pattern is disorienting from the inside as much as from outside.

### Disorganized Attachment
*concept · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The infant classification the fearful-avoidant adult style is correlated with. It was named for an absence rather than a presence: where avoidant infants consistently disengage and anxious infants consistently escalate, these infants showed no coherent strategy in either direction — moving toward the caregiver, then freezing or turning away.

  - derived_from → Mary Ainsworth (https://youtu.be/_gCOo_vQM54?t=58)

### Distorted Emotion And Distorted Logic
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The clean statement of the mirror. Under pressure anxious patterning trusts the feeling and arranges reasoning to fit it; avoidant patterning trusts the reasoning and arranges feeling to fit that. Neither is available to the other in the moment, which is why one partner offering to correct the other's logic reads as a refusal to believe them.

### Double The Work, Double The Reward
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

The fearful-avoidant runs both patterns and so has both jobs: find where the pain receptors are muted and sensitize to what is being felt but not registered, and learn to regulate in the areas where the pain is already loud and constant. Priebe adds that the identity confusion — am I the tough one or the needy one — is itself a symptom of running both.

### Doubling Down Under Stress
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Ambiguity and external threat are precisely when co-regulation is worth most, and precisely when both parties revert hardest — the avoidant to control or detachment, the anxious to fixation, each aimed at the other. Priebe's alternative is not agreement but alliance: this situation is hard, our needs differ, neither of us has to be shamed for that, and it helps to have someone to hold on to.

### Dulled Pain Receptors
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Priebe's analogy for the avoidant end: being unable to feel physical pain looks like an advantage and is disabling, because pain is the alerting system — stop, this is damage, rest. Emotional pain does the same job. It flags when the thing you are doing is wrong for you and when someone is treating you badly, and a system that mutes it loses the warning, not just the discomfort.

### Dynamic Maturation Model
*concept · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

An alternative account in which many infants classed disorganized are better read as running a sophisticated strategy fitted to a bad environment. Its premise is that a child is always adapting as well as it can to what it is given, so behaviour should be read by what it is trying to achieve rather than how it looks.

### Earned Secure
*concept · literature · secure=secure-form*

Security arrived at through deliberate work rather than received in childhood. She argues the two are not interchangeable as models: both end up in the same place by routes that have almost nothing in common, and the person who got there the hard way can describe the road.

### Emotional First Aid, Modelled
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form*

What Priebe identifies as the real difference between the secure and the anxious childhood: not whether the child was soothed, but whether anyone was seen handling their own distress. Secure children watch a parent go into discomfort and come out of it, and acquire the sequence. Being comforted without ever seeing that leaves you able to be regulated and unable to do it yourself.

### Emotionally Organised Versus Temporally Organised
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Priebe's account of why the same argument reads so differently from each side. The anxious system organises reality around felt experience: what is true about this situation is what I am feeling. The avoidant system organises it around sequence: what is true is the order of events that produced the state. Neither is lying. They are indexing reality on different keys, and each reads the other's key as an evasion.

### Emotions Accumulate From Small Signals
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Feelings are usually the compound of many minor pieces of information rather than the product of one undeniable event. This is why the evidentiary test fails: it demands a single blatant cause that most real emotions do not have.

  - contrasts_with → Rationalizing The Feeling Away (https://youtu.be/zv7ROoYCi6s?t=476)

### Emotions As Currency
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Her framing for what an infant's emotional display actually is: the only means it has of purchasing care. Crying buys soothing, anger buys an injustice being noticed, fear buys protection. An avoidant childhood is one where that currency was consistently refused at the counter, so the child learned to obtain things by not offering it.

  - source: How Does An Avoidant Attachment Style Develop? @228s — https://youtu.be/zv7ROoYCi6s?t=228

### Empathy Without Being Overwhelmed
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form · sign of change*

Neither drowning in another person's pain nor keeping away from it in case you would. Priebe attributes it to having been contained as a child — a caregiver who saw the pain, reflected it back and was not themselves capsized by it. She notes that one common use of the word empath describes the anxious version instead: unable to tell what is theirs and what is yours, so it all has to be felt.

### Enlightened Witness
*concept · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

A person who can be present with a feeling that was never met well the first time. She frames this as why the anxious route to healing cannot be walked alone: shame in particular does not survive being seen, and it is not survivable in isolation either.

*concept · literature · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Merging to the point where there is no clear line between two people. She distinguishes it sharply from intimacy: with no dividing line you have no vantage point from which to see the other person, so what feels like maximum closeness is actually the loss of the position closeness requires.

### Equally Comfortable In And Out Of A Relationship
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form · sign of change*

A preference either way is fine; what marks security is that the sense of self does not change much between the two, and that being partnered does not require hiding any part of it. Priebe adds the practical consequence — secure people compromise, but choose relationships where the compromises improve the life, and leave early when the values plainly do not match rather than spending years on it.

### Expectation
*concept · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Something you want another person to do. She is emphatic that these are not the problem — relationships run on them — but that they only function once both people have explicitly agreed. An expectation held privately and enforced silently produces exactly the frustration people mistake for a boundary being violated.

### External Locus Of Control
*concept · literature · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The state of having no reliable way back to equilibrium that does not run through another person. She frames self-regulation as its remedy and describes it less as a technique than as a relationship with yourself — one where you are accountable to, trust, and respect the person doing the regulating.

### False Attribution
*concept · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

A feeling that arrived earlier and unnoticed finds a plausible cause later in the day and fastens onto it. Her worked example runs from an unflattering photo in the morning to a partner's harmless like in the afternoon — on an ordinary day a flicker of irritation, on this one apparent proof. The logic can be wrong while the feeling is entirely real, and usually old.

### Fearful-Avoidance Is Not Anxious Plus Avoidant
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Priebe calls this the single biggest misunderstanding in attachment theory. Having both anxious and avoidant traits does not make you fearful-avoidant, because everybody has both. What makes the style its own thing is a chronic disorientation about direction — am I going toward love or toward independence — combined with distrust of yourself and of everyone else at the same time.

### Feelings Are Data, Not Noise
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The stance that emotion should be subtracted from a decision because it is irrational. Priebe's objection is practical rather than moral: people behave emotionally, so a model that omits emotion predicts badly. Removing feelings from the equation does not produce a cleaner answer, it produces a blind spot in the answer.

  - part_of → Toughness Versus Strength (https://youtu.be/_UVZHhWTX5Y?t=300)

### Fighting Fair
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form*

Not an absence of conflict — she is clear that conflict is a healthy part of living alongside someone. What changes is that it becomes bearable. Neither person feels the whole relationship riding on this argument, so it can wait: both can cool down, think, and come back to it as two people against the problem rather than against each other.

  - characterizes → Secure (https://youtu.be/WKof0naxYLM?t=79)
  - contrasts_with → Identity Threat (https://youtu.be/WKof0naxYLM?t=79)

### First-Time Vulnerability Raises The Stakes
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Doing something for the first time — admitting you hurt someone, expressing anger, asking for something — costs far more than it looks like from outside, because the skin under that dressing has been covered for decades. So an imperfect response lands twice as hard, and the partner usually has no idea a threshold was crossed at all. Priebe's caution is that the expectation of a perfect reply is quietly unrealistic.

### Flexible Responsiveness
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form*

The payoff of having been responded to flexibly: more than one setting. Space for someone who needs space, reassurance for someone who needs reassurance, rather than one strategy applied to everyone. Each insecure style, by contrast, learned a single response system and runs it regardless of who is in front of them.

### Flight Is Also Enmeshment
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Avoidant people often claim other people's moods do not affect them, and Priebe's correction is precise: the moods affect them heavily and trigger flight rather than fight. Wanting out of the room is a physiologically aroused state, not a neutral one. So the avoidant is as entangled in the other person's emotion as the anxious partner — the difference is the direction of travel.

### Getting Needs Met Without Stating Them
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Priebe's compact definition of an insecure strategy: whatever you learned to do to get a need met without saying what the need is. The secure alternative is not a personality trait but an expectation — that stating it plainly will work — which holds because secure people mostly end up with people for whom it does.

### Grief Postponed, Not Avoided
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

After a breakup the avoidant machinery reports that nothing is wrong: it meant little, I am fine, I am strong. Then a crisis or a chance meeting arrives and the whole thing lands at once. Priebe traces the deficit to the original wound — the source of the pain was the attachment figure, so the pain had to be concealed from the only person who could have helped process it, and grieving was never learned.

### Guilt Versus Shame
*concept · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Guilt says I made a mistake; shame says I am one. Priebe notes the distinction is not universally agreed among theorists, and argues it matters specifically for attachment work because the two feelings move you in opposite directions — one toward the person you affected, one away from everyone.

### Handing Over The Finished Solution
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Believing the partner is not competent to help means never bringing them an unfinished problem — so the work is done alone and delivered as a conclusion. Priebe describes a partner who, after their first argument, produced a long letter explaining why he needed to step well back; her reply was, why not just talk about it and find a new balance. He looked at her as though she were speaking another language, and then they did exactly that.

### Healing Is Not Swinging To The Other Pole
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

A guardrail she states explicitly at the close. If you are anxiously attached, the goal is not to go stoic and stop expressing anything — that is trading one insecure adaptation for the other. The target is the middle: emotion and reason both online, and interdependence rather than either codependence or counter-dependence.

### Healthy Dependency
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form · sign of change*

Total dependency is a problem; so is refusing to rely on anyone for anything. Priebe puts security in the middle: trusting people to do what they said, outsourcing accordingly, and renegotiating when it stops working. It rests on explicit agreements and on taking people at face value about what they can and cannot do — which does not prevent being let down, only makes it legible when it happens.

### History Not Ideals
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Your stated criteria come from the conscious mind; who you actually choose comes from underneath it. So the reliable evidence about what you are looking for is the pattern across the people you have picked, not the description you would give of your ideal.

### Holding Both Programs
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form*

What distinguishes the secure version. The threat response is not absent — the same costs get logged — but it runs alongside the appreciation instead of replacing it, which is what makes an actual negotiation possible.

### How Common Each Style Is
*concept · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Roughly half to sixty per cent of people are securely attached; anxious and avoidant each account for something near twenty per cent; fearful-avoidant is the rarest by a wide margin. Priebe cites the base rates specifically as a check on self-typing — the styles people most often claim are not the ones most people have.

### How Is This Adaptive In Our Dynamic
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Insecure couples argue about who is right; secure ones have a working sense of context. Priebe's replacement question, asked together: how could this behaviour be adaptive inside the relationship we have built? Explosions may be what a person resorts to when the low-volume version is never integrated. Withdrawal may be what happens when parts of someone get quietly declined every time they arrive.

### Hyper-Awareness Of Power Dynamics
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

A running background calculation in every relationship — friendship, work, romance — of what each person wants and what each has to withhold. Priebe notes it usually never surfaces as a thought; it shows up as who you can relax around. Attraction with uncertain reciprocity is uncomfortable for exactly this reason: you want their approval and they do not need yours, so the position has to be improved before anything can be risked.

### I Am Okay, You Are Okay
*concept · literature · secure=secure-form*

The secure position, and she gives it a precise content rather than leaving it as a slogan: the assumption that everyone is behaving reasonably given what they have been through. Someone can be plainly not okay and still be intelligible — which is what stops their state from being read as illogical simply because it is not yours.

### Identity Separate From The Reaction Pattern
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

The shift from experiencing a reaction as evidence about who you are to experiencing it as something running in you. She flags it as unusually load-bearing for fearful-avoidant people, whose default reading is that they are simply bad or incapable of love rather than conditioned — and it is the move that makes the rest of the work survivable.

### Impact Regardless Of Intent
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The capacity to hold that someone may have wanted things to be otherwise and that you were left unprotected anyway. Avoidant recall tends to run the two together, so a good explanation for why something happened is taken as evidence that it did no harm.

### Insatiable Anger As A Trauma Signal
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

A test Priebe uses on her own anger: if the problem in front of you were solved right now, would the anger stop? If not, it is not a response to this situation, and expressing it here will not discharge it. She treats that as the marker separating a trauma trigger from genuine present-tense anger, which is worth expressing and does resolve.

### Integrated Logic And Emotion
*concept · literature · secure=secure-form*

The secure form, and in the DMM the reason its secure category is called balanced: emotion informs what to do and reasoning informs what the feeling means, both online at once rather than in alternation.

### Integration, Not Addition
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Why this style's blind spot is structurally unlike the other two. Avoidant patterning is missing emotional information and anxious patterning is missing the analytic kind, so each has a side to develop. Fearful-avoidant has both already — and can only run one at a time. The work is not acquiring anything, it is using both at once, which is exactly what secure people do when they decide which to weight in a given moment.

*concept · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The line she draws at the end: two people who can each hold themselves and choose to lean on one another are interdependent. Two people looking to each other for everything are not intimate but dependent — she calls it an addiction to being regulated by someone else rather than closeness.

### Internal Working Model
*concept · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The template for what relationships are and what you must do to get needs met, laid down before roughly age three when the brain is wiring fastest. It is not a memory but an expectation, and it is self-confirming: what you expect of people is largely what you go on to find.

### Intimacy Requires Boundaries
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Her central reframe here: noticing where you end and someone else begins is not an obstacle to intimacy, it is the precondition for it. Only from a separate position can you understand what things are like for another person as distinct from what they are like for you — which is what seeing someone actually consists of.

*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

The fearful-avoidant is most themselves alone and can stay single a long time, then wants the emotional closeness of a committed relationship without surrendering any control over their routines, interests or direction. Priebe's contrast is with the secure position: knowing what you want, and choosing to give some of it up because sharing a life averages out better than not.

*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

A correction she is insistent about. Avoidant regulation is not someone feeling the pull to call a friend and refusing it — that description fits anxious or fearful-avoidant patterning resisting itself. ### Knowing The Mechanism
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Her answer to why understanding the origin matters at all, given that understanding changes nothing by itself. Without knowing where an impulse comes from you cannot anticipate it, so change has to be attempted blind and in the moment. Knowing the mechanism is what makes it possible to tell when the old response no longer fits the situation.

### Limerence
*concept · literature · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Believing the version of someone you assembled, in the face of evidence about the actual person. She quotes an observation that a crush is really a shortage of information — everyone fills the gaps, and the difference is whether the filling survives contact with facts.

### Look At The Motivation, Not The Behaviour
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The rule Priebe says she has re-recorded this video repeatedly to get right. Every style borrows behaviour from every other: anxious people feel avoidant in the wrong relationship, avoidant people feel anxious about losing the one arrangement that lets them function as they prefer, secure people feel both when the situation warrants. Typing by behaviour, or even by feeling, gets you nowhere. The motivation underneath is the only thing that separates them.

### Looking For A Parent, Not A Partner
*concept · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Priebe's account of why the pairing is so reliable. A good parent does not burden a small child with their problems, so the avoidant's aura of having nothing going on reads, to an anxious nervous system, as exactly the figure it has been looking for — more so than a secure person visibly working through their own material. The problem is that the parent is not a parent and has no intention of endlessly meeting needs.

### Love Addiction And Detox
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Priebe's account of the fearful-avoidant cycle in the language of addiction: hooked despite knowing it is bad, then out and genuinely sober for a long stretch, then the thought that a relationship could be handled casually now — and back in. She distinguishes it from the anxious version, which craves the same drug without the adverse reaction, and notes that substance problems are common at both avoidant ends for the same reason.

### Love Is The Medicine
*concept · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

With a compromised system, love does what the missing immunity cannot — it lets you function in a way you cannot manage alone. Secure people need it too and have it circulating already, through friendships and family they can reach for. The anxious version is desperation, because the dose is doing structural work, and the supplier is a single person.

### Making A Wrong Relationship One You Fit
*concept · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The cost of the whole tactical repertoire, stated plainly: if you will use every available means to keep someone present who does not authentically want to be, you succeed in making a relationship that is wrong for you into one you are well adapted to. The adaptation is real. So is the wrongness.

### Meaningful Goals And Collaboration
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form · sign of change*

Setting a goal that means something needs both faculties: the emotional one that knows what speaks to you, and the practical one that knows what makes sense. Priebe's marker is not that secure people never get this wrong, but that they do not have a lifelong structural weakness at either end — they can direct their own life and merge it with someone else's, and count both kinds of goal as real.

  - characterizes → Secure (https://youtu.be/u203fXLJ79w?t=1150)

### Mentalizing
*concept · literature · secure=secure-form*

Holding that another person's mind runs on different contents than your own — that something can be fine by you and not fine by them. It begins coming online around age four and keeps developing for life. Priebe's point is that guilt depends on it, which is why guilt is the later and more elaborate of the two feelings.

### Meta-Feelings About The Oscillation
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Fearful-avoidance is not only anxious triggers plus avoidant triggers. Because the system keeps switching, each state passes judgment on the other: the deactivated self is ashamed of what the activated self felt and said, and the activated self feels guilty about the distance the deactivated self wanted. Priebe treats this second layer as the distinctively fearful-avoidant part.

### Missing The Off Switch
*concept · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The anxious counterpart. The pain registers fully; what is missing is the mechanism that ends it. Priebe's image is a stubbed toe that keeps hurting, harder and harder, until somebody else arrives to stop it — at which point wanting someone permanently within reach stops looking like insecurity and starts looking like a reasonable precaution.

### Mistyping Into The Middle
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Fearful-avoidant is the category people place themselves in when they can see both anxious and avoidant behaviour in themselves but cannot yet tell the two apart. Secure people land there too, because a secure person does feel anxious when there is something to be anxious about. The discriminator is not the mix of behaviours but whether they fire when the situation warrants them.

  - contrasts_with → Fearful-Avoidant (https://youtu.be/AMUN9M9H3U4?t=165)

### Mutual Trust
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form*

Standing on two legs rather than one. Both people know where they stand — barring something extreme, nobody is leaving — and both know they would survive it if they did. Her image is a bird untroubled by the branch, because what it is relying on is its own wings.

  - characterizes → Secure (https://youtu.be/WKof0naxYLM?t=292)
  - contrasts_with → Chronic Abandonment Fear (https://youtu.be/WKof0naxYLM?t=292)

### Navigating By Rules Instead Of Attunement
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Where the glue between people was never shared feeling, a child builds a rulebook instead: if she looks happy this morning, approach; if not, keep clear. It works, so it generalises — behaviour observed, patterns learned, risk of rejection minimised. The blindspot is not the method's accuracy but its omission: nothing in it involves being in emotional contact with anyone.

### Needing The Medicine And Allergic To It
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

A severely compromised system and an allergy to the only treatment. Priebe adds the detail that makes it worse: the painkillers do not hold for the fearful-avoidant the way they do for the dismissive. So the need surfaces anyway, the dose is taken, the reaction follows, and there is no version of the arrangement that works.

### Needing The Person You Are Angry At
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

At the top of the scale the fearful-avoidant system runs two incompatible programmes at once: get the anger out, and get this person on side so they will help bring me down again. Priebe traces it to never having learned down-regulation from anger in childhood — the only route back to baseline runs through someone else, and the only person available is the one being shouted at.

### Negative View Of Self, Positive View Of Others
*concept · literature · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The classic anxious position, and the engine behind idealisation. Reading it as seeing the best in someone is the flattering version; the mechanism is closer to assigning qualities you need them to have, then meeting the real person as a disappointment.

### No Stable Centre Of Gravity
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Priebe puts numbers on it. The anxious person sits at roughly eighty per cent outside themselves and twenty per cent grounded; the avoidant runs the inverse; the fearful-avoidant hovers near the middle with no settled answer. Hence the practical paralysis — no stable view on whether to invest in relationships or in self-work, because whichever you chose last week was chosen by a different configuration.

### Nobody Is Required To Give You Their Attention
*concept · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

A child has a survival claim on a parent's attention, and the tactics that enforce that claim are legitimate at four. An adult partner has no such obligation: they may decide not to care, not to love you, and to walk away in the moment you need them. Priebe states it without softening, because the tactics only make sense while the claim is assumed.

### Nobody Made That Experience Matter
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

A phrase Priebe took from a speaker at a workshop, describing a close family member dying in childhood: nobody made that experience matter. It is the caregiver's job to see the child's interior and connect it to what has happened — you feel grief, you feel loss, those are the right responses to this. Where that does not happen, the feeling arrives with no place to sit.

### Not A Personality Type
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Why the usual personality-system habits do not transfer. Those frameworks assume the type is fixed, so the useful move is to celebrate your quirks and work with your natural energy. Attachment styles are changeable, and what is dominant in an insecure one is mostly the part that is not working — so treating it as an identity to embrace inverts the point of knowing it.

### Not Taking Moods Personally
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form · sign of change*

There are two ways to take a mood personally: reading it as rejection, or being irritated that someone is displaying what you have learned to suppress. Priebe's secure version is neither — curiosity at a slight distance, an offer of help if it is within reach, and otherwise carrying on, because their state genuinely is not about you.

  - characterizes → Secure (https://youtu.be/u203fXLJ79w?t=220)

### Not Your Fault, But Your Responsibility
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The principle she puts at the centre of the whole endeavour, and the one most often split in half. People collapse the two clauses together — if I did not cause it, then fixing it is not mine to do — and the framework becomes an explanation for staying as you are. Both halves have to be held at once: you did not choose the patterning, and you are the only one who can change it.

  - source: How Not To Use Attachment Theory @481s — https://youtu.be/vlL6L7Cck-c?t=481

### One Root, Many Symptoms
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Procrastinating at work, picking fights, eating when you are not hungry — apparently unrelated until you notice they all run when you feel insecure. Priebe's argument for the slowness of stage two is that noticing across enough areas is what lets you find the root, and that solving the root retires the symptoms without having to be fought one at a time.

### Openness Without Self-Protection
*concept · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The anxious imbalance. She is careful to name the strength first and rate it highly: a real openness to being taught and changed by loving someone, which she says is genuinely unavailable to much of the avoidant spectrum and is required for a secure partnership. Unbalanced it leaves a person entirely undefended — her image is an infant lying open-armed in a cot, an energy that works precisely because someone else is doing the protecting.

### Others Meet You As Deeply As You Have Met Yourself
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Priebe names this as the most profound shift of her own attachment work: going from a bodily certainty of existential aloneness to a bodily belief that she could be known. The order mattered. Uncovering the no-go areas in her own psyche was what made it possible to communicate herself to other people at all — a thing she had previously experienced as impossible rather than difficult.

### Over- And Under-Taking Responsibility
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Activated, the fearful-avoidant is owed things and the partner is failing them. Deactivated, they cannot reach the emotion they were in, look at their own conduct through a cold analytic lens and conclude they must be the abusive one. Priebe is careful on both sides: they genuinely can be, as any insecure style can, and the deactivated verdict is not more accurate for being calmer. The disorientation is the diagnostic feature.

### Overwhelm And Judgment Are The Boundary Signal
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

An avoidant system does not present a clear sense of what is needed — it presents overload, distress, and a judgement about the other person. Priebe reframes all three as the same message: a boundary is required here. The judgement is not a verdict on them, it is the notification.

### Pain Hidden From Yourself
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Her correction of the usual stereotype, and an important one: this is not someone concealing pain from other people. When it reaches conscious awareness they process it about as well as anyone. The trouble is that it largely does not arrive — frustration and contempt surface in its place, and once out of the activating moment the memory loses most of its emotional charge. Better for analysis, useless for learning.

### Pain Is The Central Axis
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Priebe's reframe of the whole system. Attachment is usually described as how you relate to other people; she argues the load-bearing variable underneath is how you process emotional pain. Nobody is exempt from it — the difference between the styles is what happens once it arrives, and most of the outward behaviour follows from that.

### Painkillers Instead Of Medicine
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Unable to take the medicine, the avoidant takes analgesics: overwork, drink, substances, food, compulsive escape into fiction. Priebe's objection runs through an Advil advert she saw — pain says you can't, Advil says you can — which she reads as exactly wrong. Pain is the indicator, not the problem. Silence it and you keep using the injured arm.

### Parallel Support
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form*

Her picture of what adult intimacy looks like: two people moving alongside each other, each responsible for their own healing, offering support across that separation. The alternative she contrasts it with is two people facing each other and treating the other as the solution — which is the arrangement the fantasy is built around.

### People-Pleasing Is A Barrier To Intimacy
*concept · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The anxious system reports that accommodating will bring you closer. It does the opposite: it deletes the interesting, differing parts of you and puts a reflection of the other person in their place. Nobody enters a relationship wanting themselves mirrored back. The more either person pleases, the less there is in the room to be close to.

### Phobia Of Inner Experiences
*concept · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Certain emotional states have no regulation attached to them, so the system redirects before they arrive. Priebe's examples are specific: anger begins in the body and a freeze response takes over; sadness begins and attention suddenly has to be somewhere else, online, researching, anywhere. It reads as distraction. It is a flight response, and the information in the feeling never lands.

### Powerless Over Others
*concept · literature · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The premise Priebe rates as the single most useful thing an anxious-spectrum person can accept. If you truly could not influence what someone thinks or feels about you, the whole repertoire becomes pointless — and what appears in its place is the set of questions you have been avoiding: is this the right person, is this situation safe for me, what would a better option look like?

### Predictability Restores Calm
*concept · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Why a named time settles a nervous system that an open-ended promise cannot. Her analogy is a hungry child told repeatedly not yet, versus one told they will eat when you get home in three quarters of an hour — the second can wait, because the question has changed from whether to when.

  - contrasts_with → Chronic Abandonment Fear (https://youtu.be/T09X0_6mP3Q?t=481)

### Presence And Curiosity Versus Strategy And Analysis
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

A child who was met with presence and curiosity copies it: they meet people as blank slates and let what is unique to each connection emerge. A child who was not has to find another route, and the route available is analysis — working out in advance who this person is, what they would like, and who to be for them. Both feel like paying close attention. Only one is attending to the actual person.

### Projecting Your Own Remedy
*concept · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Seeing a partner withdraw, the anxious system reads it through its own machinery: if I withdrew, it would be to draw someone closer — so they must need love. And so love is delivered, in quantity, to someone who was asking for space. Priebe names the trap: this is how you can give continuously, receive nothing back, and conclude you are being undervalued, while never once giving the thing that was wanted.

### Promises Made By A Self You Cannot Guarantee
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Commitments get made sincerely by one configuration and come due to another — the career built on emotional openness that becomes unbearable the week vulnerability is actually required, the resolution to be emotionally healthy that dissolves on the next activation. Priebe's point is that the resulting self-distrust is well-founded, and that awareness of the pattern makes decisions harder before it makes them easier.

### Protection And Comfort
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The two things attuned care supplies, and the distinction that organises the whole model. Protection resolves the cause so it is less likely to recur, and includes the unwelcome limits that prevent future pain; comfort meets the fact that some of it is hard regardless. Each insecure style turns out to have received one and not the other.

### Psychic Equivalence
*concept · literature · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The assumption that the intensity of your feeling measures the badness of your situation. Priebe uses it to explain a pattern she sees constantly: an anxious person in an emotional flashback feels overwhelmingly awful, concludes the awfulness must be coming from the person in front of them, and reaches for toxic, gaslighter, narcissist. The positive version does the same work in reverse, and produces idealisation.

### Punishing Humility
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

A partner arrives with an apology and gets the other ten unaddressed items, or a speech about how unacceptable it all was. Understandable — humility from them is rare, so the window feels precious — and it reliably ensures the next one does not come. Priebe's wider version: an environment hostile to mistakes does not produce fewer mistakes, it produces less honesty about them.

### Rational And Emotional, But Never At Once
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

The fearful-avoidant has access to distorted emotion like the anxious and distorted logic like the avoidant, and no integration between them. Priebe describes the effect on the people around them: a friend who can set out precisely why the relationship cannot work, and keeps choosing it — because the analysis was done deactivated and the decisions are made activated, and neither state can reach the other.

### Reading People Easily
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Having learned early that what people say is unreliable, the fearful-avoidant reads everything else — and gets genuinely good at it. Priebe knows one who became a world-class poker player on exactly that skill. What distinguishes it from anxious hypervigilance is comfort looking at their own manipulations, which makes other people's legible too. The blind spot is secure people, whose lack of strategy reads as a strategy being concealed.

  - characterizes → Fearful-Avoidant (https://youtu.be/5jk7PAa8D1o?t=2950)

### Realistic Cause And Effect
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form*

The secure position between the two distortions: neither authoring everything that happens to you nor being at the mercy of everyone else. It means checking whether you are being taken advantage of, setting boundaries where you are, and otherwise engaging in good faith.

  - source: How Does An Avoidant Attachment Style Develop? @1202s — https://youtu.be/zv7ROoYCi6s?t=1202

### Realistic Expectations Of A Relationship
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form*

The one she calls most important. Insecurity brings expectations a relationship cannot meet, and the relationship then buckles under them. Her image is hunting for milk in a hardware store — the disappointment is guaranteed by the premise, and no amount of effort inside the shop fixes it.

### Regressing To Child And Parent In Conflict
*concept · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

When the connection feels threatened, the anxious system stops seeing another adult with needs of their own and starts seeing a parent — someone to be placated by abandoning your position, or fought hard to be heard at all. Priebe is clear that conflict with people you love is dysregulating for anyone; the tell is the shift in who you think you are talking to.

### Regulating With The Idea Of Each Other
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Priebe's account of why insecure couples produce enormous fights: both are relating to the picture of the other person, and to a picture of how a relationship should go, rather than to what is in front of them. Attunement is the corrective not because it prevents disagreement but because it catches divergence early — a chasm cannot open quietly between two people who are actually in the present moment together.

### Relationships As Resource
*concept · priebe · secure=secure-form*

Seeing a relationship as something that supplies you rather than only draws on you. Until it is a resource, the sacrifices it asks for have no rationale and will read as pure loss.

  - source: Avoidant Attachment: When Attraction Turns Off Without Warning (Unpacking Deactivation Triggers) @1212s — https://youtu.be/7mElEzMpbeE?t=1212

### Relief Mistaken For Joy
*concept · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Her central move in this video, built on a pair of images. Live with a low-grade headache long enough and painkillers start to feel sublime — but the best available state was never the pill, it was not having the headache, and you have no way to tell the difference from inside. Live hungry and food becomes the whole world; eat properly and your attention is free for everything else. The highs of insecure attachment are relief from a chronic background of not being good enough, and relief is temporary by construction.

### Repressed Emotion Breaks Through Harder
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

An anxiously attached person is in continuous contact with their subtler feelings; a fearful-avoidant is not, and may go through a day unaware of how much is running underneath. Priebe's observation is that the emotion which does break through can therefore land harder than the anxious version of the same feeling, precisely because everything below it stayed down.

### Repression Versus Suppression
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Suppression is knowing a need is there, choosing to set it down for now, and intending to come back to it — renting while you save for the house you know you want. Repression puts the need somewhere you cannot find it, so you keep moving and feel vaguely wrong without ever locating what you are missing. Both look like going without; only one leaves the need retrievable.

### Resolution Versus Regulation
*concept · priebe · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

Mid-argument, the question worth asking is which goal is running. Advocating a need and hearing theirs is one thing; getting them to make you feel better is another, and the second quietly replaces the first without announcing itself. It sounds like: how do I get them to see how much pain I am in. The points you came in with are usually the casualty.

### Responding To The Past In The Present
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Meeting a current situation with emotions belonging to an old one — furious that a partner cannot read a need that went unmet in childhood, or that they failed to give space you never asked for. Priebe's point is that most insecurely attached people do this continuously while taking the reaction as an accurate reading of the present, and that catching it is the whole of the first step.

### Rigidity Is Adaptive At Seventy Per Cent
*concept · priebe · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Without reliable feedback about what keeps you in connection, anything that works seven times in ten deserves to be run every single time — it is the best available bet. That is why insecure relating goes rigid, and why the other three times in ten keep producing the same damage. Priebe's point is that the rigidity is intelligent, and that it stops being intelligent once feedback becomes available.
